# Harriet Ainslie

## Overview

- **Status:** alive  _(assumed)_
- **Family:** [Clementine Ainslie](../character/clementine-ainslie.md) (sibling), [Lionel Fairlie](../character/lionel-fairlie.md) (spouse), [Lorna Vane](../character/lorna-vane.md) (relative)

## Appearance

Harriet Ainslie is a woman of great beauty, possessing a dark, swarthy countenance and a large build. She has black hair accompanied by bushy, dark eyebrows, and her eyes are a steel-blue shade that resembles the slaty blue of gulf waters. In her own stern, dark-eyebrowed manner, she presents a handsome appearance.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER XIII. THE HOUSE ON THE HILL P25](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0025), [v5 CHAPTER XXII. ST. LAURENCE KNOWS ALL ABOUT IT P8](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0008), [v5 CHAPTER XXII. ST. LAURENCE KNOWS ALL ABOUT IT P38](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0038), [v5 CHAPTER XXVI. MISS WINIFRED GETS A NEW POINT OF VIEW P17](../source/v05-c26.md#nw-v05-c26-p0017)_

## Personality

Despite a somewhat severe facial expression, Harriet possesses a cheerful disposition and is known for her robust laughter and sharp-talking, expertly narrated tales. An avid reader, she harbors a intense aversion to isolation, resorting to speaking her thoughts aloud to bypass unwanted loneliness. Consequently, she is deeply motivated to ensure that [Clementine](../character/clementine-ainslie.md) keeps her vow not to marry, fearing that being left entirely alone would prove unbearable and break her mind.

## History

Following her mother's death, Harriet Ainslie resided in her old home, experiencing intense despondency and suppressing her younger sister, [Clementine](../character/clementine-ainslie.md). When [John Ashdown](../character/john-ashdown.md) visited their home and engaged Harriet in a lively political discussion, Harriet warned [Clementine](../character/clementine-ainslie.md) of his romantic intentions and reminded her sister of a promise she had made. As Ashdown prepared to propose, Harriet readied herself to hold [Clementine](../character/clementine-ainslie.md) to a past vow to reject him. After [Clementine](../character/clementine-ainslie.md) revealed Ashdown's proposal and begged to be released from her vow never to abandon her, Harriet steadfastly refused, compelling her sister to send Ashdown a cold written rejection. Later, after [Clementine](../character/clementine-ainslie.md) agreed to release Harriet from her own vow so that Harriet could marry [Lionel Fairlie](../character/lionel-fairlie.md), Harriet insisted that she would not marry Lionel unless [Clementine](../character/clementine-ainslie.md) lived with them.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER II. SHEER GOSSIP P66](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0066), [v5 CHAPTER XIII. THE HOUSE ON THE HILL P5](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0005), [v5 CHAPTER XIII. ## Quotes

> "Pay attention to what I say, Mr. Ashdown, because that person will end up in a battle eventually. He craves it. He will cause an absolute sensation."
>
> — Harriet Ainslie — [v5 CHAPTER XIII. THE HOUSE ON THE HILL P27](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0027)

> “I take your word for it!” agreed Miss Harriet. “Pay attention to what I say, Mr. Ashdown, because that person will end up in a battle eventually. He craves it. He will cause an absolute sensation.”
>
> — Harriet Ainslie — [v5 CHAPTER XIII. THE HOUSE ON THE HILL P27](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0027)

> "I shall refrain from doing it. To me, a pledge remains a pledge. I shall refrain from doing it. Violate your own word—commit perjury if you so choose—yet it will occur without any agreement from me."
>
> — Harriet Ainslie — [v5 CHAPTER XXII. ST. LAURENCE KNOWS ALL ABOUT IT P28](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0028)

> "I do not understand what would stop you. The size of his house is sufficient—you would possess your own portion of it—he would not intrude."
>
> — Harriet Ainslie — [v5 CHAPTER XXXII. TWO STUBBORN PEOPLE P39](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0039)

> “Well, he might court in that manner,” Harriet replied. “I gather that men employ all sorts of methods. However, Clementine, remember what you promised.”
>
> — Harriet Ainslie — [v5 CHAPTER XIII. THE HOUSE ON THE HILL P34](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0034)

### [Clementine Ainslie](../character/clementine-ainslie.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/clementine-ainslie--harriet-ainslie.md)

[Clementine](../character/clementine-ainslie.md) is Harriet's sister, but their relationship becomes deeply strained over Clementine's suitors. Harriet fiercely holds [Clementine](../character/clementine-ainslie.md) to a past vow never to abandon her, suspecting John Ashdown's romantic intentions and ultimately refusing to release [Clementine](../character/clementine-ainslie.md) from the pledge when Ashdown proposes. Even after [Clementine](../character/clementine-ainslie.md) later consents to let Harriet marry [Lionel Fairlie](../character/lionel-fairlie.md), Harriet stubbornly insists she will not marry Lionel unless [Clementine](../character/clementine-ainslie.md) agrees to move in with them.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER II. SHEER GOSSIP P66](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0066), [v5 CHAPTER IV. THE MANSE CHILDREN P50](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0050), [v5 CHAPTER XIII. THE HOUSE ON THE HILL P24](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0024), +21 more_

### [John Ashdown](../character/john-ashdown.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/harriet-ainslie--john-ashdown.md)

Harriet shares a close intellectual friendship and good companionship with [John Ashdown](../character/john-ashdown.md), often engaging him in lively political discussions regarding [Germany](../codex/places.md#germany) and the Kaiser when he visits their home. However, tension arises because Harriet recognizes his romantic interest in [Clementine](../character/clementine-ainslie.md) and actively works to thwart it. She holds her sister to a vow never to abandon her, ultimately causing [Clementine](../character/clementine-ainslie.md) to send Ashdown a cold rejection that leaves him heartbroken.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER XXI. THE IMPOSSIBLE WORD P8](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0008)_

- Friend of — close intellectual friendship and good companionship  <sub>[v5 CHAPTER XXI. THE IMPOSSIBLE WORD P8](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0008)</sub>

### [Lionel Fairlie](../character/lionel-fairlie.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/harriet-ainslie--lionel-fairlie.md)

Harriet is engaged to [Lionel Fairlie](../character/lionel-fairlie.md), rekindling an old courtship with him. After pondering her feelings for Lionel at a party, their path to marriage hits an obstacle due to Harriet's insistence on maintaining her sisterly pact. Even when Lionel confronts [Clementine](../character/clementine-ainslie.md) to successfully gain her release of Harriet from the vow, Harriet refuses to marry Lionel unless [Clementine](../character/clementine-ainslie.md) comes to live with them.
